title: Claim Limits, Suspension and Reinstatement on the Keyturn Guest Protection Plan
content:
How many losses a level of the Keyturn Guest Protection Plan will meet, how quickly the guest must report
an incident and answer questions on a claim, and what count of settled losses closes the level to the guest are
all written into the level. The reporting window is the hours after an incident within which the guest must
report it; the cooperation days are the calendar days the guest has to answer questions on a claim against
them; the claim limits are the claims the level will meet on one trip and for one guest in a rolling year; the
suspension count is the number of losses settled against the guest in a rolling year at which the level closes
to them; and the waiting period is the calendar days a suspended guest waits before electing that level again.

| Protection level | Incident reporting window (hours) | Days to answer questions on a claim | Claims met on one trip | Claims met in a rolling year | Claims in a rolling year that close the level | Waiting period before electing again (calendar days) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Keyturn Declined Protection | 24 | 7 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 180 |
| Keyturn Minimum Protection | 24 | 7 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 120 |
| Keyturn Standard Protection | 24 | 10 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 90 |
| Keyturn Advantage Protection | 48 | 14 | 2 | 4 | 5 | 60 |
| Keyturn Premier Protection | 48 | 14 | 3 | 5 | 6 | 45 |
| Keyturn Business Traveler Protection | 72 | 21 | 3 | 8 | 10 | 30 |

## The schedule read the other way about

The two lowest levels of the Keyturn Guest Protection Plan are the quickest to require a report, at 24 hours,
and the slowest to reopen, at 180 and 120 calendar days. Keyturn Standard Protection also requires a report
within 24 hours but reopens after 90 calendar days. Keyturn Advantage Protection and Keyturn Premier Protection
allow 48 hours to report, and Keyturn Business Traveler Protection 72. The days allowed to answer questions on
a claim run 7, 7, 10, 14, 14 and 21 up the ladder.

## Hypothetical counts read against the schedule

A guest with 3 losses settled against them in the rolling twelve months stands at, and not below, the
suspension count written for Keyturn Minimum Protection, which is 3, and below the counts written for Keyturn
Standard Protection, Keyturn Advantage Protection, Keyturn Premier Protection and Keyturn Business Traveler
Protection, which are 4, 5, 6 and 10; the count written for Keyturn Declined Protection is 1. On one trip,
Keyturn Declined Protection meets 0 claims, Keyturn Minimum Protection 1, the next two levels 2 each and the
top two 3 each; in a rolling year the same six levels meet 0, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 8.
